newsitem.title: USA: Officer cleared in black man's death promoted.
newsitem.headline: Officer cleared in black man's death promoted.

text.p: A white police officer acquitted last year in the death of a black motorist was promoted this week from patrolman to sergeant, police officials said Wednesday.

Sgt. John Vojtas, an officer in the Pittsburgh suburb of Brentwood, was acquitted last November of involuntary manslaughter in the death of Jonny Gammage, who died along a roadside in October 1995 while in the custody of five white policemen.
Three of the officers, including Vojtas, were charged with involuntary manslaughter.
Gammage, 31, was the cousin and business partner of former Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals, who now plays for the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Gammage's parents, who live in Syracuse, New York, issued a brief statement in reaction to Vojtas' promotion. "There is something wrong with the justice system," they said.
Following his trial, Vojtas had been reinstated as a patrolman on Brentwood's force. He had been a policeman for 16 years.

The other officers who were charged, Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland and Baldwin Patrolman Michael Albert, had their charges dismissed last month by Allegheny County Judge David Cashman, who presided over Vojtas' trial.
Allegheny County District Attorney Bob Colville has said he plans to appeal.

The cause of death was listed as suffocation caused by compression to the neck and chest. The incident began when Mulholland pulled Gammage over early in the morning of October 12, 1995, for what he said was erratic driving.
Mulholland said Gammage became violent after leaving his car as the other officers were arriving to provide backup.
The officers testified in a coroner's inquest that they had to hold Gammage face-down on the ground to restrain him. Gammage died at the scene.
